title: DecisionTraceBench: Tracking Decision-Critical Information in Multi-Party Spoken Conversations
abstract: arXiv:2610.34746v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In high-stakes domains such as finance, critical information evolves through multi-party interaction. Recovering these changes and their sources is fundamental to reliable speech understanding. Existing speech benchmarks focus on transcription, local understanding, and turn-level state prediction, leaving joint decision evolution across speakers insufficiently evaluated. We introduce DecisionTraceBench, a speech state-tracking benchmark for Decision-Critical Information State Tracking (DCIST). It jointly evaluates decision event sequences, speaker attribution, scope, and temporal evidence, using trajectory-level F1 to measure complete event-chain recovery. Our dataset comprises Chinese financial dialogues involving two to four speakers, with 100.39 hours of synthetic audio and 8.61 hours of human-performed recordings. translated_title: DecisionTraceBench：多方口语对话中决策关键信息的追踪
translated_abstract: 在金融等高风险领域中，关键信息通过多方交互不断演化。恢复这些变化及其来源是实现可靠语音理解的基础。现有语音基准主要聚焦于转录、局部理解和轮次级状态预测，对跨说话人的联合决策演化评估不足。我们提出了DecisionTraceBench，一个面向决策关键信息状态追踪的语音状态追踪基准。该基准联合评估决策事件序列、说话人归属、范围和时间证据，并使用轨迹级F1分数来衡量完整事件链的恢复程度。我们的数据集包含涉及两至四位说话人的中文金融对话，包括100.39小时的合成音频和8.61小时的真人录音。在固定的真人录音子集上，五个级联系统和两个直接音频模型取得了DCIST分数……（摘要截断）
tldr: 提出DecisionTraceBench基准，面向多方中文金融语音对话中的决策关键信息状态追踪（DCIST），联合评估决策事件序列、说话人归属、范围和时间证据，并以轨迹级F1衡量完整事件链的恢复能力。
en_tdlr: Introduces DecisionTraceBench, a speech state-tracking benchmark for Decision-Critical Information State Tracking (DCIST) in multi-party Chinese financial spoken dialogues, jointly evaluating decision event sequences, speaker attribution, scope, and temporal evidence using trajectory-level F1.
